questions.question: What are the penalties for a DUI conviction?
questions.explanation: A DUI conviction can result in a fine, jail time, loss of your license, and payment for emergency services.

questions.question: In Virginia, what must all passengers under 18 do?

options.text: Wear a seat belt only in the front seat.
Wear a seat belt only in the back seat.
Wear a seat belt in any seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a seat belt in any seat.
questions.explanation: The driver must make sure all passengers under 18 use a seat belt or child safety seat, no matter where they sit.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Then quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross first. Pay attention when driving through intersections or turning.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you see it. Trains cannot yield to cars, so you must wait for them to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before turning.

questions.question: The driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that the driver is not paying full attention.

questions.explanation: Stay focused while driving. Don't talk to passengers, look for items, or daydream. If another driver seems distracted, keep extra distance because they are more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is at the next intersection ahead.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and wait before driving.
Honk your horn and pass the bus on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done leaving the bus.
Pass the bus before it opens its door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait before driving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops and puts out its stop arm, you must come to a complete stop. Do not drive until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop for other drivers or pedestrians. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: In a crash, move your car off the road and stop if you can. If anyone is hurt, call 911. Report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone is killed, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means you should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic enter your lane.
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign shows that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.

questions.question: You must let right-of-way go to:

options.text: People walking across a street or highway.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing at crosswalks or intersections. You must also yield to funeral processions and military convoys. Do not cut through them or join them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to pass before you go.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on a highway, you should:

options.text: Go to the next exit and turn around there.
Ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit and turn around there.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Before driving a car you have not driven before, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it since all cars are the same.
Not tell your friend that you do not know the car.
Ignore any problems so you do not embarrass your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how to use them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how to use them.
questions.explanation: When driving a new car, take time to find and practice the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A triangular red and white yield sign means slow down at the intersection. Let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Pay special attention where children are present. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are crossing in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Which substance can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?

options.text: Controlled substances, such as illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants, such as glue or paint

questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
There are a series of curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired or intoxicated is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely when you drink alcohol or take drugs. Driving under the influence is dangerous to you and to others on the road.

questions.question: What is true about worn or bald tires?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase your stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without enough tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: How should you drive safely at night?

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights are working properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take steps to make driving safer for yourself and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective thing you can do to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not pass if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (in this case, 13 feet, 6 inches).

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need a longer distance to stop and may skid when turning quickly. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive with care.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of death increases. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic can also be dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.
